key_insight: The paper compares direct and indirect PINN formulations for Dirichlet boundary control of semilinear parabolic PDEs, and provides a conditional error analysis showing how indirect PINNs can be monitored through residual-based estimates.
engineering_relevance: This matters for PDE-constrained control problems because it offers a PINN-based workflow for optimizing boundary actuation while quantifying when the learned control and state are likely trustworthy.
method: Direct PINN: separate networks for state and control, trained by minimizing a penalized tracking objective.
Indirect PINN: joint networks for state, adjoint, and control trained on the first-order optimality system.
Error framework: decomposes total error into approximation, optimization, quadrature, and soft boundary/terminal-constraint terms, with a computable residual indicator.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on two manufactured test problems, including a cubic reaction-diffusion equation and a linear case with nontrivial boundary control and adjoint behavior.
watch_item: The main error and reliability guarantees are conditional, relying on regularity, approximability, soft-constraint control, and a local neighborhood assumption around the reference solution.
paper_title: Direct and Indirect Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dirichlet Boundary Control of Semilinear Parabolic Equations: A Conditional Error Analysis
